title: Gurbaz Smashed His Fastest Century. It Took Shubman Gill 66 Balls to Make It Irrelevant.
excerpt: In a rain-soaked 25-over contest at Dharamsala, India chased down 195 with 13 balls to spare. Debutants Gurnoor Brar and Harsh Dubey each took three wickets.
body:
Dharamsala had a monsoon haircut before the toss. Persistent overnight rain shaved the first ODI between India and Afghanistan down to 25 overs a side — essentially a T20 with an extra five overs of breathing room. What followed was a breathless contest that rewarded aggression, punished timidity, and offered two captains a useful set of notes ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup cycle. For the Indian diaspora across the US, UK, and Canada, these matches are more than just a game; they are a vital thread connecting them to their roots, sparking lively discussions in community groups and family chats, and often dictating weekend plans as they tune in from different time zones.

Afghanistan lost the toss and lost three wickets for 26 runs inside four overs. On most days, that scoreline is a death sentence. But Rahmanullah Gurbaz does not read scorecards the way most openers do.

## Gurbaz Turns the First Innings on Its Head



> **"“It was kind of a Twenty-20 game,” Gill said after the match."**


Left alone at the crease after Ibrahim Zadran (1), Sediqullah Atal (0) and Rahmat Shah (3) fell cheaply to Arshdeep Singh and debutant Gurnoor Brar, Gurbaz treated the situation not as a crisis but as a licence to attack. Alongside captain Hashmatullah Shahidi — who played the anchor role with a patient 27 — Gurbaz stitched a 116-run partnership off just 66 balls that rewired the innings entirely.


![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)


His fifty came off 25 balls. His century came off 48 — the fastest by any Afghan batter in ODI history, and his ninth overall in the format. Eight sixes and eight fours peppered the Himalayan outfield before Nitish Kumar Reddy knocked over his middle stump with the score at 135 for 3.

“It was kind of a Twenty-20 game,” Gill said after the match. “Gurbaz batted brilliantly... but I think the way we pulled back in the middle and the death overs was brilliant.”

## The Debutants Deliver

India’s reply to Gurbaz’s onslaught came not from their established names but from two men playing their first international match. Gurnoor Brar, the Punjab-born seamer who had waited patiently through the IPL, dismissed Zadran with his very first over — a length delivery that moved away late, drawing an edge that Gill pouched at mid-off. Brar finished with 3 for 27.
